articles.title: 3 Must-Play September Games You Missed Between Fire Emblem and Wolverine
articles.summary: Congratulations: You’ve almost made it through one of the busiest Septembers in video game history! For anyone who enjoys keeping up with new games as they come out, September has run a ceaseless pace.
body: Those big-name games were only the tip of one gigantic iceberg, though. September was filled with lesser-known indie gems that are worth coming back to if you ever manage to finish Fortune’s Weave. From cozy puzzle games to excellent Metroidvanias, these three September deep cuts make for a much-needed cooldown between hours of hacking and slashing.
A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

If you’re the kind of person who frequents review aggregate sites like Opencritic, you may have been shocked this week to see that Well Dweller is currently one of the best reviewed games of 2026. That was less surprising to those who are already familiar with the work of developer Kyle Thompson. The mind behind last year’s lovely Crypt Custodian has put together another strong twist on the Metroidvania formula with the fairytale-like Well Dweller. If you’re looking for something that has the vibe of Hollow Knight: Silksong minus the crushing difficulty, Well Dweller is a more approachable 2D action game that’s still complex enough to please fans of the genre.

articles.title: The 10 Best Fights in 'Jujutsu Kaisen' History, Ranked
articles.summary: MAPPA’s adaptation has continued raising the bar with each successive arc. Season 1 established the fundamentals through Yuji Itadori and Aoi Todo’s exhilarating teamwork and Satoru Gojo’s casual displays of near-godlike power.
body: Jujutsu Kaisen has never treated a fight as mere spectacle. The anime ’s best battles reveal how their participants think under pressure, turning elaborate cursed techniques into tactical puzzles that expose a character’s strengths, fears, and capacity for improvisation. The result is one of the most kinetic battle shonen ever made — and one in which “strength” can mean something entirely different from one confrontation to the next.

That constant escalation makes ranking the anime’s fights difficult. An early confrontation involving Yuji or Megumi Fushiguro naturally feels smaller than the deadly contests awaiting them in the Culling Game, while Sukuna ’s destructive battle with Mahoraga may eventually be eclipsed by what the anime’s upcoming fourth season has in store. For now, however, these are the 10 best fights in Jujutsu Kaisen, ranked from great to greatest for their animation, tactical ingenuity, and character-defining consequences.
points: MAPPA’s adaptation has continued raising the bar with each successive arc.
Season 1 established the fundamentals through Yuji Itadori and Aoi Todo’s exhilarating teamwork and Satoru Gojo’s casual displays of near-godlike power.

articles.title: Star Wars Nabs Spider-Man Director Jon Watts for First Movie in Disney's New Skywalker Saga Trilogy
articles.summary: Disney has reportedly picked Spider-Man director Jon Watts to helm the first movie in Simon Kinberg's new Star Wars trilogy as it plots out the next chapter in the Skywalker Saga.
body: Information about a new series of Star Wars projects from Lucasfilm was first reported by Daniel Richtman and later corroborated by The Hollywood Reporter. Although Watts is best known for leading the charge on the Marvel Cinematic Universe's Tom Holland Spider-Man trilogy, his work on Star Wars would represent his return to the sci-fi franchise following his time as co-creator on 2024's Skeleton Crew.

The yet-to-be-named new films, which are said to be the next chapter in the Skywalker Saga, are being written by Star Wars: Rebels and Mr. and Mrs. Smith veteran Kinberg. Story details remain mostly shrouded in mystery, though it's said that Daisy Ridley's sequel trilogy Jedi, Rey Skywalker, will play a role in the story.

Watts has only been picked to direct the first movie of the new trilogy so far. When this next chapter will begin is also unclear, with The Hollywood Reporter sources noting that Disney has not given the new project the official green light as work on its foundation continues.
points: Disney has reportedly picked Spider-Man director Jon Watts to helm the first movie in Simon Kinberg's new Star Wars trilogy as it plots out the next chapter in the Skywalker Saga.

articles.title: DC's Groundbreaking 170-Episode Action Series Is Waiting to Be Discovered on Free Streaming
articles.summary: The CW has produced more than its fair share of DC superhero shows over the years, from The Flash and Supergirl to Legends of Tomorrow and Black Lightning. Some remain favorites in their own right, while others became memorable for just how wonderfully weird the shared universe eventually became.
body: That same ambition extends to the show's special effects and massive set pieces. Although the CGI doesn’t hold up next to modern blockbusters, Arrow regularly attempted large-scale stunts that could have been far more embarrassing on a television budget. What makes such action sequences special is how they’re often inextricably tied to the show's emotional stakes and dual-narrative structure.

Perhaps no scene highlights this better than the epic season 2 finale showdown between Oliver and Slade Wilson (Manu Bennett). The masterful editing seamlessly weaves back and forth between their sword-swinging deathmatch in the island flashbacks and their present-day brawl through Starling City, anchoring the spectacular choreography in years of deeply personal betrayal. Whether he was clashing with formidable villains like Malcolm Merlyn (John Barrowman) or relying on the tactical support of trusted allies like John Diggle (David Ramsey) the action in Arrow was the physical manifestation of Oliver's arduous journey from a hardened survivor to a genuine hero.
points: The CW has produced more than its fair share of DC superhero shows over the years, from The Flash and Supergirl to Legends of Tomorrow and Black Lightning.
Some remain favorites in their own right, while others became memorable for just how wonderfully weird the shared universe eventually became.

articles.title: 5 Detective Shows to Watch If You Love 'Lanterns'
articles.summary: The show has already established its merits, thanks to a measured slow-burn approach that thrives on the central duo’s riveting chemistry. Although chock-full of comic book references and superhero-isms, Lanterns shines brightest when it leans on its murder mystery elements.
body: HBO’s ongoing detective show Lanterns has already proven itself exceptional. Created by Chris Mundy ( Ozark ), Damon Lindelof ( Watchmen ), and comics writer Tom King, Lanterns follows veteran Green Lantern Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler) and new recruit John Stewart (Aaron Pierre), who will eventually occupy Hal’s mantle. Together, they investigate a dark murder mystery in Rushville, Nebraska, which gradually exposes a cosmic conspiracy.

If Lanterns has ignited a love for detective shows, you're in luck. There are countless great series out there worth checking out (although most don't have magic rings and exploding aliens). Here are five shows to watch once Lanterns ends and you still need a dose of hard-boiled mystery drama.

articles.title: Godzilla Minus Zero Review
articles.summary: Review: Godzilla Minus Zero doesn’t disappoint in the slightest on the kaiju front, but does lack the same level of emotional resonance that its predecessor held.
body: This review is based on a screening timed to the New York Film Festival. Godzilla Minus Zero opens in theaters in Japan on November 3 and in North America on November 6.

Godzilla movies have long had a problem: What do you do after the initial thrill of a quote/unquote serious Godzilla origin story? Can the filmmakers somehow continue the deep thematic underpinnings of that first adventure, even while upping the visual ante with more giant monster action? How do you offer a probing commentary about the world we live in – which is what the best of the genre is known for – when you’ve got skyscraper-sized lizards slugging it out MMA-style?

It is under these circumstances – or should I say restrictions? – that Godzilla Minus Zero enters the ring. As the sequel to the much-praised Godzilla Minus One from three years ago – a picture that dealt with, among other things, notions of survivor’s guilt, hope in the face of hopelessness, found family, and more – Minus Zero is on the ropes from the start. Can returning writer-director Takashi Yamazaki wring even more out of his characters, who have already been to hell and back, while also blowin’ up stuff real good? In a word, no.
points: Review: Godzilla Minus Zero doesn’t disappoint in the slightest on the kaiju front, but does lack the same level of emotional resonance that its predecessor held.

articles.title: Minecraft still gains around 300,000 new players a day, Xbox boss reveals
articles.summary: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma says Minecraft still gains over 300,000 new players a day, as Minecraft Live reveals Dungeons II and a Switch 2 port.
body: More than 300,000 try Minecraft for the first time every single day.
That's according to Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, who announced on Twitter/X over the weekend that despite 17 years and 425 million copies sold, "Minecraft is still finding new players".
"Today at Minecraft Live: Dungeons II, our first new dimension in more than 14 years, new ways for creators to build, Minecraft on Nintendo Switch 2, and more," she wrote.

"More than 300,000 people play Minecraft for the first time on an average day. After 17+ years and 425M+ copies sold, I love that Minecraft is still finding new players and giving longtime ones new things to discover."
points: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma says Minecraft still gains over 300,000 new players a day, as Minecraft Live reveals Dungeons II and a Switch 2 port.

articles.title: Microsoft CEO Says 'Streamlining' at Xbox is 'Great to See' as Layoffs Affect Thousands
articles.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has spoken about the state of Xbox following layoffs that affected thousands of workers, saying that the "streamlining" at the company is "great to see." The tech executive opened up about how the business' gaming branch is doing during a recent interview on the Sources…
body: When touching on Xbox's place under the grander Microsoft umbrella, Nadella said he feels "fantastic" about the IP the brand has in its portfolio and its "ability to take that and produce great games going forward." As layoffs continue to reshape the developers who have made some of those great games, he still seems to be feeling pretty good.

"There's a certain amount of streamlining the team is doing and [Xbox CEO Asha Sharma] is doing, which is great to see," Nadella said in the wake of the most recent cuts. "And then, we have to invent the right sustainable business model that allows us to deliver gaming to more and more people.

"That has always been the goal, which is, we want to be a great publisher and a great platform provider for games across both PCs and Xboxes. So, that is our goal, and I think Asha and team have said that Xbox is going to get back to growth this next fiscal year, and that's the plan they're executing on, and in that process, do a bang-up job of producing some great games."

articles.title: Minecraft Is Getting Its First New Dimension In Over 15 Years
articles.summary: Announced today during Minecraft Live, Mojang is adding the first new dimension to the blocky sandbox game in more than a decade and a half. The Sift is an ethereal-looking fourth dimension that was first marketed for Minecraft Dungeons 2, and it's now been confirmed that it's coming to the base…
body: The Sift is a major new addition for Minecraft, marking the first new dimension since 2011's The End, where players go to fight the Ender Dragon in the end game. Speaking to GameSpot, Minecraft Dungeons 2 creative director Mans Olson explained that the team wanted to make sure that The Sift felt distinct from the Nether and The End rather than becoming another hostile environment.
"We wanted to make sure that it was different. That it doesn't feel like the ones that already exist in the game," he confirmed.

Unlike the Nether and The End, where the environments feel immediately hostile thanks to dangerous environmental hazards and angry mobs, the developers wanted it to feel like somewhere players could potentially live.
That doesn't mean that The Sift will necessarily always be completely safe. In Minecraft Dungeons 2, the dimension is under threat from the Illagers, leaving its ecosystem in danger.
points: Announced today during Minecraft Live, Mojang is adding the first new dimension to the blocky sandbox game in more than a decade and a half.

articles.title: The Next Minecraft Update Adds Ice Caves, A New Mob, And More
articles.summary: Minecraft's next game drop will add a new underground environment to the sandbox game, along with a new hostile mob, and items that bring frosty mechanics to exploration and combat.
body: Announced during Minecraft Live on September 26, the upcoming game drop is expected to follow the usual drop cadence of once per quarter, releasing in December 2026. Its biggest addition is ice caves--a rare underground extension of Minecraft's existing cold biomes.

Ice caves will add more environmental variety to cold areas, giving you another reason to venture underground when exploring snowy regions. The caves will also contain ice crystals, which can be collected and used for decoration. Ice crystals can be placed vertically or horizontally, and they'll also produce light, giving you another way to illuminate your creations.

However, ice caves aren't entirely peaceful. A new hostile mob in the form of the Frozen Zombie will lurk underground, bringing new combat mechanics with it. Frozen Zombies can apply a stacking freezing effect with their melee attacks. If you take too many hits you'll eventually freeze, making getting surrounded by Frozen Zombies especially dangerous. They can also throw ice balls, which deal damage and knock players back.
points: Minecraft's next game drop will add a new underground environment to the sandbox game, along with a new hostile mob, and items that bring frosty mechanics to exploration and combat.

articles.title: The next retro games coming to Steam are a pair of extremely 1990s run-and-gunners where Spanish Goku fights mutants
articles.summary: Jody's first computer was a Commodore 64, so he remembers having to use a code wheel to play Pool of Radiance. A former music journalist who interviewed everyone from Giorgio Moroder to Trent Reznor, Jody also co-hosted Australia's first radio show about videogames,
body: In the 1990s, Spanish videogame label Gaelco was responsible for a string of arcade games (and also electronic dartboards) that hardly anyone outside Spain knows about, bar perhaps the occasional breakout like World Rally.

Retro specialists QUByte Interactive are bringing two of Gaelco's obscurities to Steam this year, resurrecting arcade action games Thunder Hoop and its sequel TH Strikes Back. The genetically engineered and oddly named Thunder Hoop of the title is a hand-blasting hero who fights armies of mutants unleashed by the evil Dr Genbreak.

The original Thunder Hoop, from 1992, is a platformer in which the teenage hero has to fight cartoonish monsters across a cityscape that includes the obligatory sewer and underwater levels. The 1994 sequel ages him up to a beefcake adult who has heard of shirts and thinks they're for cowards, and includes a lot more run-and-gun action against women in latex, and a sequence where he goes Super Saiyan than flies into space for a Gradius-style scrolling shooter bit.

articles.title: Between 70 and 80% of Blood Bowl 3 games were solo
articles.summary: You'll know this frustration if you've ever been part of the community around a game that has both singleplayer and multiplayer modes. People who prefer one to the other are always convinced the other cohort doesn't exist.
body: In the case of the Blood Bowl videogames, the fact the CPU's tactics are so rudimentary has always given people who prefer the multiplayer mode ammunition for claiming the other half doesn't exist. Now we've got proof they're actually the majority. As Cyanide programmer Mathieu Valero recently told Wargamer, between 70 and 80% of Blood Bowl 3 games were played solo in Eternal Leagues.

This came up in the context of Blood Bowl 3's imminent replacement by Warhammer Blood Bowl. One of the improvements, Valero suggests, will be the AI. "We didn't have an AI—now we do", as he put it. "There are still a bunch of factions and builds that it's more able to play well: you want to give it Guard and Block, and don't go fancy with the combos that a human would be able to do", he went on to say, but "give something reliable to the AI, and you're gonna have a game to play".

articles.title: Microsoft CEO says Xbox's "streamlining" is "great to see" despite cuts and layoffs
articles.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has praised Xbox's ongoing "streamlining" under Xbox CEO Asha Sharma just days after another round of layoffs hit the division.
body: Speaking on the Sources podcast with Alex Heath, Nadella was asked about Xbox's ongoing overhaul and the state of the brand and said he felt "fantastic".

"I feel fantastic about the IP we have right now," Nadella said (as transcribed by IG ). "If I look at the studios, the IP portfolio we have, and our ability to then take that and produce great games going forward - I feel fantastic. There's some amount of streamlining the team is doing, and Asha is doing, which is great to see."

He continued: "And then we have to invent the right sustainable business model that allows us to deliver gaming to more and more people. That has always been the goal, which is we want to be a great publisher and a great platform provider for games across both PCs and Xboxes.

"So that is sort of our goal, and I think Asha and the team have said that Xbox is going to get back to growth this next fiscal year, and that's the plan they're executing on, and in that process, do a bang-up job of producing some great games."

articles.title: Former Elder Scrolls designer Kurt Kuhlmann on Fallout: New Vegas diehards: 'I don't know that Todd wanted to create that situation again for The Elder Scrolls'
articles.summary: I want to establish my old school RPG sicko bona fides really quick: My favorite Fallout games are 1 and New Vegas. My least favorite is 3 (4 is better than it gets credit for in critical circles). I really did not like Starfield and did not make it past the first planet.
body: With that out of the way, it is deranged how a lot of fans talk online about Bethesda as a studio, and Todd Howard as a guy. I have no doubt as to the accuracy of Kuhlmann's assessment of his former boss.

And I don't blame Howard one bit for being protective of the series in this way⁠. It's pretty relatable, and I'm sure it wasn't the only consideration around avoiding mainline-style spinoffs, as Kuhlmann's thoughts on ESO indicate.

Reading this in bad faith, you could parse it as an admission of weakness or insecurity, but I don't see it that way. I've spoken to senior Bethesda devs myself and watched them in other interviews: They're proud of their own work, speak positively of New Vegas, and seem to respect their peers at Obsidian. I think it's YouTubers impugning their character or calling for their coworkers to be fired over a perceived mishandling of the series that gets on their nerves.

Fallout memers seem to have gotten what they wanted, but in a monkey's paw kind of way. Obsidian is making a new Fallout game now, but with a gun to its head. Given all the layoffs and studio closures Xbox has under its belt, with more no doubt on the way, it doesn't feel like anybody's winning.
points: I want to establish my old school RPG sicko bona fides really quick: My favorite Fallout games are 1 and New Vegas.
My least favorite is 3 (4 is better than it gets credit for in critical circles).
I really did not like Starfield and did not make it past the first planet.
With that out of the way, it is deranged how a lot of fans talk online about Bethesda as a studio, and Todd Howard as a guy.

New game drops, developer insights, Minecraft Dungeons II, and some extra special announcements – it’s all coming up!
Once it’s over, stick around for the Deep Dig After Show where our developers and guests delve deeper into some of the new features.
Tune in on September 26th at 10am PT / 1pm ET / 6pm BST / 7pm CEST.

videos.title: Dawngazer - Ignisphere Teaser Trailer
videos.summary: Presented by Takafumi Noma director (character designer, and scenario writer of Unicorn Overlord and former veteran of Vanillaware) × Good Smile Company, the new IP brand "IGNISPHERE" has officially launched.
body: We are excited to release this teaser trailer introducing an epic original world woven together by numerous nations and races.
■ New Game Currently in Development!
The first game based on the IGNISPHERE universe, an all-new Action RPG titled "DAWNGAZER," is currently in development.
